thread:
nidhi: Quick check — thinking about privacy-preserving metering. Can we redact raw tokens from the billing pipeline but still keep accurate token counts and attribution for audits?

sam: Do you mean remove token text entirely before we write to the event stream? :thinking_face:

nidhi: Yeah. Idea: ingest only token counts + a per-tenant HMAC or blinded fingerprint instead of plaintext. Keep provenance (request id, model, route) but not the transcript.

mike: That would reduce PII surface. But for audits where we need to replay prompts for quality/regression, how would we rehydrate?

nidhi: Two options: 1) store encrypted transcripts in a separate, KMS-backed store (retention short) accessible only via an audit flow; or 2) store irreversible digests + a time-limited re-identification capability via a key escrow.

jess: Option 2 sounds scary legally unless we lock the escrow process. Option 1 seems simpler operationally.

alex: We also have to consider cost & throughput. Extra KMS operations per request kill us at scale. If we encrypt transcripts, need batching of KMS wraps or a cache of data keys per pod.

sam: For counting/billing we don't need tokens themselves, just counts and attribution metadata. Could we compute per-request counts at the edge and scrub token text before the mid-tier?

mike: For attribution we need stable tenant key or fingerprint to join events across services. HMAC(token_text, tenant_salt) could provide stable but irreversible IDs. That still leaks patterns if tenant_salt is stable and attacker has lots of inputs.
nidhi: Right. Threat model: internal devs with access, third-party subpoenas, and accidental leak. Goal: minimize plaintext copies; allow controlled audit only with appropriate approvals.

jess: Proposal sketch: - Edge computes token_count, token_summary_digest = HMAC(SALT, first_k_token_hash || last_k_token_hash || len) - Stream gets token_count + digest + provenance - Transcripts encrypted with per-tenant DEK, stored in audit bucket with strict IAM & 30d TTL - Audit flow requires ticket + access review to fetch and decrypt with KMS.

sam: That reduces KMS calls (only on object write/rotate). But how do we handle canary / eval workflows that call for batch replay of prompts? 30d may be too short for long-term experiments.

mike: We could support an opt-in archival retention for customers who authorize longer retention (enterprise agreements). Default 30d to minimize risk.

alex: Practical detail: the token_summary_digest must be stable across replays to allow linking generation events with any later eval event that also captures digest. Edge compute must use deterministic pipeline for digest components. Document the exact concat format.

jess: Also add a per-deployment salt rotation policy. If salt rotates, joins fail. We need a migration scheme: keep previous N salts for join window.

sam: What about aggregation for billing windows? We can aggregate counts without storing any digest at all; billing only needs counts per tenant per window. Digests are only needed for audit correlation.

nidhi: True. Maybe keep two paths: "billing path" (counts only) and "audit path" (digests + encrypted transcripts). Audit path is rate-limited and stored with strict controls. Billing path flows through our normal streaming ingestion for SLA.

mike: Edge-case: streaming responses where tokens arrive incrementally. We need to ensure counts are final and attribution consistent. If we redact at edge, include final_count when the stream closes. For partial failures, fallback to server-side counting which will see no raw tokens — need robust handshake to mark which side counted.

alex: Handshake flag idea: event has field counted_by: [edge|server] and final_count boolean. That'll help reconcile.

jess: Add replayability requirement to audit: auditors can request decrypt within audit UI; audit API records approver and returns redacted transcript plus original only if allowed. Keep an immutable audit log entry for every decrypt.

sam: Operational question: how do we prove to customers that counts haven't been tampered with if we don't keep plaintext? Merkle roots or signed aggregated checkpoints?

nidhi: We can publish signed daily aggregates (per-tenant) that include token_counts and checksums of audit digests. That provides tamper-evidence without exposing tokens.

mike: Implementation notes: - Edge: minimal CPU for HMACs (fast) - Collector: accept counts + digest, dedupe by request_id - Storage: compressed counts + encrypted object references - Audit UI: long-poll for approval, KMS decrypts object key, returns transcript - Monitoring: missing decrypt attempts, failed KMS ops, volume of opt-in long-retention tenants

alex: Performance sanity: HMACing first/last k token-hashes needs token hashing on edge. We should benchmark on smallest instance types. Also watch CPU credit burn for bursty customers.

jess: Security review needed: key rotation, least-privilege IAM roles, separation of duties for audit access. Bring sec/compliance into RFC.

sam: Can we prototype a minimal PoC just for internal trials? Edge SDK adds a flag to emit digest + counts and an opt-in archiver for transcripts.

nidhi: Yes. PoC scope: 2-week spike. Goals: show 0 extra per-request KMS calls, measurable reduction in text retention surface, and a working audit decrypt flow.

alex: I'll spin up a test plan: 1) Edge SDK change + unit tests 2) Collector schema changes + compatibility flags 3) Encryptor service for transcripts + background uploader 4) Audit UI stub 5) Cost/latency benchmarks

mike: I'll add a small CLI to run bulk decrypt tests against KMS and record audit log entries.

jess: I'll take security owner for the PoC and draft an initial threat model doc.

infra-bot: Deploy status: new PoC branch created: github.com/redwood/ingest/tree/feature/privacy-metering-poc (deployed to sandbox). :rocket:

nidhi: Thanks all — let's sync Wed 11am to review PoC plan and acceptance criteria. I'll create a short RFC with the options and the proposed default (counts-only billing + encrypted audit transcripts). :+1:

sam: Sounds good. Add a note about analytics teams who currently rely on full transcripts — need migration plan.

mike: Also flag partners who pull raw streams today. We'll need a partner transition policy.

jess: Filing: I'll open a ticket in SEC-OPS for key management policy and another in ENG to track the PoC tasks.

nidhi: Awesome. Closing thread for now — comments on the RFC welcome once I post. :slightly_smiling_face:
